q1: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, SUM(C.CREDITS) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING SUM(C.CREDITS) > 10 AND COUNT(C.CREDITS) > 5
q2: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, SUM(C.CREDITS) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING SUM(C.CREDITS) > 10 AND COUNT(C.CREDITS) > 8

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they differ in the HAVING clause. Q1 filters groups where the sum of credits exceeds 10 AND the count of credits exceeds 5, while Q2 filters groups where the sum of credits exceeds 10 AND the count of credits exceeds 8. These conditions are different, so the resulting groups may differ.
counterexample_dsp: A department with 6 courses totaling 12 credits will be included in Q1 but excluded in Q2 since COUNT(C.CREDITS) = 6 > 5 in Q1 but 6 <= 8 in Q2.
